title: Commercial backflow testing: scope access, assets, and filing together
description: Use the official requirement and exact assembly record first.
prompt: What should be verified before this backflow work is scheduled?
answer: Use the official requirement and exact assembly record first. Confirm the device, system use, responsible party, field scope, test result, and report filing as distinct steps.
urgency: Escalate when a deadline, active leak, damaged assembly, critical service, or authority approval is involved.
identifiers: Verify the exact assembly, size, system use, and property record.
Use the governing utility or authority for the final requirement.
Keep testing, repair, and submission records together.

choices.label: I have an official notice or requirement
choices.detail: Match it to the exact property and assembly before booking work.

choices.label: The device failed or needs service
choices.detail: Define repair, retest, and filing responsibility separately.

choices.label: I need a complete scope
choices.detail: Include access, testing, closeout, and documentation in the comparison.

steps.title: Identify the record
steps.body: Match the property, assembly, model, size, system use, and official requirement.

steps.title: Define the complete scope
steps.body: Separate field work, access, testing, repair, reporting, and approval responsibilities.

steps.title: Close the documented loop
steps.body: Retain the completed outcome and official confirmation with the site asset record.

safeChecks: Use the official issuer and manufacturer record before committing to work.
Confirm tester, contractor, and report-submission responsibility in writing.
Keep property and assembly records together.
stopConditions: Do not substitute an unverified device or workflow.
Do not treat a visit as complete before the required result and filing are confirmed.
notThisDevice: A generic product listing is not an approval record.
A different system type may require a different workflow.
This page does not replace a qualified on-site assessment.
evidenceNote: Final requirements must be verified with the governing program and exact manufacturer documentation.
